:::{#thm-deriv-matrix-vector}

#### Vector-derivative of a matrix-vector product

If $\matr{A}$ is an $m \times q$ matrix that is constant with respect to $\vb$,
and $\vecf{v} = \vecf{v}(\vb)$ is a $q \times 1$ vector
that depends on the $p \times 1$ vector $\vb$,
then:

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vb} (\matr{A}\vecf{v})}_{p \times m} =
\underbrace{\paren{\deriv{\vb} \vecf{v}}}_{p \times q}
\underbrace{\tp{\matr{A}}}_{q \times m}
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-deriv-matrix-vector-special-case}
#### The derivative of a linear map as a special case

This result generalizes @thm-deriv-linear-map,
which is the special case $\vecf{v} = \vb$
(so that $q = p$, $\deriv{\vb} \vb = \matr{I}_p$,
and $\deriv{\vb} (\matr{A}\vb) = \matr{I}_p \tp{\matr{A}} = \tp{\matr{A}}$).
For example, with $\matr{A} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vecf{v} = \vb = \tp{(\beta_1, \beta_2)}$,
$\matr{A}\vb = 2\beta_1 + 3\beta_2$,
and its vector derivative is $\tp{(2, 3)} = \tp{\matr{A}}$.

:::
